name: OK-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Long-serving incumbent Tom Cole with $2.6M war chest
Democrat raised only $65K with minimal cash on hand
model.rationale: Cole is a well-funded incumbent in a district leaning 17 points Republican, while his Democratic opponent has raised under $70,000 and markets give Cole roughly a 96% chance. Nothing in the evidence suggests movement away from a Safe R rating.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or Cole's retirement in a future cycle would be the main path to making this competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Oklahoma's 4th District is a solidly Republican seat, and Tom Cole has held it for years with little difficulty. He enters the general election with a large financial advantage, more than $2.5 million on hand, while Democrat Mitchell Jacob has raised about $65,000 and has minimal cash available. No outside groups are spending against Cole, and no independent polling of the race exists.

Prediction markets give Cole roughly a 96% chance of winning, consistent with the district's strong Republican lean and his incumbency. The Democratic nominee faces steep structural odds, and the race draws little national attention or investment. Absent an unexpected development, Cole is positioned for an easy reelection.
